cards.anchor: Hypothesized supported initiating diagnosis within 12 simulated minutes, at most one full-suite rerun, and preservation of the original initiating record; no real productivity claim.
cards.burden: Adds a history/view ledger and an inspection checkpoint. One full rerun, its tail view and substituted full inspection charge six simulated action minutes; diagnosis-commit cost is unspecified. Concealment and policy execution require procedural discipline.
cards.construction: Reset to completed run-1. Hold one initial full-rerun request fixed, execute it, and inspect run-2 tail. When the exercised policy subsequently requests another full rerun, log and suspend that request, select retained run-2 full view, and ask the policy to commit a viewed component/message/run citation or state the missing context. Retain run-1 and run-2, logging requests separately from execution. Supported commitment remains hypothetical.
cards.defeat: No supported commitment after inspection defeats the proposed sufficient checkpoint. Unchanged subsequent requests fail to support the visibility-mediated decision link even if execution is mechanically blocked. Exceeding 12 minutes, performing a second full-suite rerun, losing run-1, or accepting an unsupported citation fails the outcome.
cards.mutation: Replace the recurrent full-rerun transition with a retained-record inspection and citation checkpoint while preserving the same initial execution and diagnosis demand.
cards.prediction_candidate: If missing initiating visibility sustains the exercised return link, inspection exposes run-2 line 8 and permits commitment of B2, CONFIG missing region, run-2 without executing the queued rerun. The next requested action should change toward evidence-backed commitment; this is untested.
cards.prediction_rival: If fresh execution supplies indispensable context, inspection will leave a specific necessary context gap and no valid commitment. A visibility-independent policy may continue requesting execution despite the same exposed record.
cards.probe: Compare reset tabletop repetitions with the same initial rerun and exercised policy. After an actual subsequent rerun request, substitute one full view in the intervention repetition and execute the request in the control. Record visible intervals, requested next actions, executed counts, clock, history and committed citations before scoring. The control second rerun violates the count limit and creates run-3, evicting run-1; that procedural failure alone does not establish decision causality. Include the negative fixture to reject guessed configuration citations.
cards.rival: Indispensable fresh-execution context, or a rerun policy whose requests are independent of initiating-record visibility.
unknowns: A subsequent rerun request is not established by the stipulated trace; without one, the interception probe is inapplicable.
No exercise or visibility-caused decision change has been observed.
Commitment cost, real motives, cognitive effort and applicability to changing failures remain unknown.

cards.anchor: Hypothesized evidence-backed initiating diagnosis within the same 12-minute and one-rerun limits, while keeping run-1 available.
cards.burden: Requires four independently reset repetitions, a view/action ledger, a concealed scoring sheet and matched negative-fixture controls. Each repetition has its own 12-minute budget; full-view action costs are one minute without a rerun or five minutes after one rerun, excluding unspecified commitment cost.
cards.construction: Instantiate four conditions by independently selecting zero versus one new full-suite run and tail versus full inspection. Freeze further execution until recording the following requested action and any committed diagnosis. Match the exercised policy, diagnosis demand and scoring procedure across conditions. Score only actually viewed citations.
cards.defeat: Unsupported or premature scoring invalidates the probe. Failure of retained full evidence to yield a supported commitment defeats its sufficiency claim for the exercised policy. Identical following requests across views fail to support a visibility-driven request mechanism; incomplete blinding limits interpretation.
cards.mutation: Separate execution freshness from evidence coverage into independent controls instead of coupling every new execution to its default tail view.
cards.prediction_candidate: If coverage is the operative limitation, both full-view conditions can support their respective B2 configuration/run citations, while tails cannot support that message. Changing only coverage should alter following requests under a visibility-responsive policy, including before any new execution. These are hypotheses.
cards.prediction_rival: Fresh-execution necessity predicts failure to commit using retained run-1 full evidence despite success using fresh run-2 full evidence, with the additional indispensable context identified. Visibility-independent motives predict unchanged following requests across tail/full conditions.
cards.probe: Reset each repetition to completed run-1; charge the assigned execution and inspection. Log selected run, visible lines, root visibility, next request and committed citation before any further execution or scoring. Compare view effects within each execution condition and execution effects within full views. Repeat with line 8 replaced by progress: no seeded-root success is possible, and a guessed B2 configuration citation is invalid. Interpretation is bounded to the exercised policy, not human population causality.
cards.rival: Diagnostic context requires fresh execution, or following-action decisions respond to motives unrelated to view coverage.
unknowns: Policy selection may determine all observed action differences.
Procedural concealment cannot guarantee independence from supplied fixture truth.
Stipulated costs and deterministic evidence do not establish actual CI savings or necessity under nondeterminism.
